# Numeric predictors and probabilities

A numeric predictor can change the probability of an outcome continuously. Here we model the probability of a low post-treatment LSAS score as a function of baseline GAD-7 score (`gad_screen`). The logistic model is linear on the log-odds scale, but its probability curve is generally curved.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(marginaleffects)

df_clean <- read_csv2(here("data", "steps_clean.csv")) |>
  filter(!is.na(lsas_post), !is.na(gad_screen)) |>
  mutate(
    lsas_post_bin = factor(
      if_else(lsas_post < 50, "Low", "High"),
      levels = c("High", "Low")
    )
  )
```
:::



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
mod_gad <- glm(
  lsas_post_bin ~ gad_screen,
  family = binomial,
  data = df_clean
)
summary(mod_gad)
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Model interpretation

A one-point higher baseline GAD-7 score changes the estimated probability of a low post-treatment LSAS score by **-1.74 percentage points on average** (95% CI **-3.19** to **-0.30 percentage points**).

Because the logit link is nonlinear, a one-point probability change can differ across GAD-7 values. The coefficient in `summary()` is a log-odds change; exponentiating it gives an odds ratio, not this probability-scale slope.
:::


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
plot_predictions(mod_gad, condition = "gad_screen", type = "response") +
  labs(
    title = "Estimated probability of low post-treatment LSAS",
    subtitle = "Across baseline GAD-7 scores; 95% confidence interval",
    x = "GAD-7 score at screening",
    y = "Probability of low post-treatment LSAS"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

# From a continuous score to a curve

A linear predictor does not imply a straight line on the probability scale. For this reason, plots and predictions at clinically meaningful values are usually more informative than reporting a coefficient alone.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
gad_values <- quantile(df_clean$gad_screen, probs = c(.25, .50, .75), na.rm = TRUE)

predictions(
  mod_gad,
  newdata = datagrid(gad_screen = gad_values),
  type = "response"
)
```

# Summary

- Logistic regression can model a binary outcome using a continuous predictor.
- Probability curves are usually easier to communicate than log-odds coefficients.
- An average probability slope is an interpretable summary, but it can conceal variation across the predictor range.
